entries.note: Nature 406:203 (PMID 10910363) resolves; quote verbatim in abstract. Untested correct: rabbit HDL/CETP read-out, no human comparison in 2000. Model = cholesterol-fed rabbit, the class's pivotal model.

Circulation 105:2159 (PMID 11994249) resolves; quote verbatim (abstract only). Abstract itself names rabbit precedent then 'first results in humans', so comparison_stated=true holds. Nit: source never calls it a match, set source_calls_it=null.

Untested correct. Morehouse 2007 abstract verified (70-80% inhibition, HDL-C 207 vs 57 mg/dL, 60% less aortic lesion) and de Grooth 37% inhibition; I also found no published rabbit-vs-patient exposure comparison.
Same Okamoto 2000 source and quote as engagement 1; untested opener correct, atherosclerosis end-point is what the class built on.

NEJM 356:1304 (PMID 17387129) resolves; quote and figures (+61% HDL-C, PAV +0.12 vs +0.19%, P=0.72) verbatim in abstract; full text 403 so comparison_stated=false stays unverified-false. Keep Nissen key, not Forrest (see rule_questions 1). Judgement DOIs all verified; NCT00134173 no results.

Status fine, model wrong: the rabbit was the efficacy model; the class relied on the rat/dog/monkey safety package (seed: 'Animal safety studies'). Okamoto cannot open a safety strip; relabel the model or drop the opener as the seed does.

Re-key to Forrest 2008 (doi 10.1038/bjp.2008.229, read in full): comparison_stated=true, key sentence verbatim in Discussion, five species, rat adrenal aldosterone, anacetrapib inert at matched exposure. Barter's quote hedges against off-target; keep in judgement. Model = animal safety studies.

missing: Human genetics (test 2): Zhong 1996 (JCI 97:2917, verified: carriers RR 1.43-1.68 for CHD) is one study, not 'the' genetics prediction. The same Honolulu cohort prospectively (Curb 2004, doi 10.1194/jlr.M300520-JLR200) found carriers had the LOWEST CHD rates (n.s.), and the 2008 JAMA meta-analysis (Thompson 2008, doi 10.1001/jama.299.23.2777; 27,196 cases) found CETP-lowering genotypes weakly protective (OR 0.94-0.95 per allele). So genetics did not univocally predict the opposite of the rabbit; it was mixed through 2004 and agreed in direction with the rabbit (modest benefit, which is what REVEAL later found) by 2008. Under the brief the best model is the one relied on (the rabbit), genetics is not a preclinical model, and it was not univocal: no effect on any cell. Fix the efficacy-2 judgement wording 'Human genetics pointed the other way' to 'one study (Zhong 1996) pointed the other way; Curb 2004 and Thompson 2008 did not'.

Seed comparison (test 3), contexts/chd-cetp.json vs draft, cell by cell: (a) CONTEXT FIELDS differ: seed = Cardiovascular / 'Coronary heart disease' MONDO:0005010 ('coronary artery disorder', verified via OLS) / order 51 / label 'Coronary disease (CETP)'; draft = Metabolic / 'Hyperlipidemia' MONDO:0021187 ('hyperlipidemia', verified) / order 190 / label 'Hyperlipidemia (CETP)'. Seed is better supported: the rabbit models atherosclerosis and every comparison trial enrolled CHD / high-CV-risk patients (ILLUMINATE conditions: Coronary Disease, Diabetes; ILLUSTRATE: Coronary Disease, Coronary Arteriosclerosis, Hyperlipidemia); the draft frames by the biomarker the class moves, not the disease it was tested in. One of the two must be dropped or the class is double-counted. (b) ENGAGEMENT: seed empty; draft 2000 untested + 2002 same (de Grooth, abstract states the rabbit precedent). Draft better supported. (c) DOSE: seed empty; draft 2000 untested with verified Morehouse/de Grooth numbers. Draft better. (d) EFFICACY opener: identical source (Okamoto 2000); tie. (e) EFFICACY 2007 contra: seed keys Barter 2007 ILLUMINATE (HDL +72.1% vs baseline, death HR 1.58, both verified), draft keys Nissen 2007 ILLUSTRATE (HDL +61% vs atorvastatin, PAV null, verified). Both verbatim, same year, no strip change. Draft's is the tighter end-point match for 'did the disease respond as the model said' (rabbit aortic lesion vs coronary atheroma) and was published first (Mar vs Nov 2007); seed's is the stronger clinical contradiction. Seed note 'later CETP inhibitors also failed on HDL' is imprecise (anacetrapib RR 0.91 in REVEAL); draft's judgement is accurate on dal-OUTCOMES/ACCELERATE/REVEAL (all DOIs verified). Draft better. (f) SAFETY 2007 contra: same source in both (Barter 2007). Seed's model 'Animal safety studies' is right; draft's 'Cholesterol-fed rabbit' is wrong. Draft's judgement adds Forrest 2008, the best primary source (verified in full). Merge: Forrest 2008 key + seed's model label. (g) SAFETY opener: seed none; draft 2000 Okamoto rabbit is mis-assigned; seed's omission is cleaner unless a tox-package first-use source is found. (h) population: seed 'High cardiovascular risk', draft 'Unselected (high cardiovascular risk)'; draft follows the v2 brief. (i) note: seed empty; draft's note figures verified, and PREVAIL (NCT05202509, obicetrapib) is active-not-recruiting, primary completion 2026-11, no results, so 'had not published as of Nov 2026' holds.

Safety: the first published patient-side BP contradiction is March 2007 (ILLUSTRATE +4.6 mmHg, Nissen 2007; RADIANCE 1, Kastelein 2007, doi 10.1056/NEJMoa071359, PMID 17387131 verified), before ILLUMINATE in November. Same year, no strip change, but the judgement should say the BP signal preceded the mortality signal by eight months.

Safety: the draft's claim that no preclinical paper reported blood pressure before the trials is a negative claim I could not fully test within budget; it is consistent with Forrest 2008 calling the events 'unexpected' and framing its own work as a post-hoc search for off-target effects, so I did not challenge it.
rule_questions: Juxtaposed vs stated comparison for `contra`: the house examples (ad-amyloid Doody 2013, Egan 2019) key `contra` to the trial paper with no model named (comparison_stated=false), but the checker brief says a `contra` with no published model-vs-patient comparison should be `untested`. Which governs? It decides whether efficacy stays Nissen 2007 or moves to Forrest 2008 (whose Introduction states 'preclinical studies with CETP inhibitors demonstrated beneficial antiatherosclerotic effects in animal models' immediately before ILLUMINATE's 'unexpected increase in cardiovascular events and death', though against events, not atheroma, and with no single <=40-word sentence carrying both sides), and whether safety is Barter 2007 or Forrest 2008. I recommended: efficacy keep 2007 (house precedent, tighter end-point), safety re-key to 2008 (Forrest's own data make the comparison). If strict rule 1/5 wins, both move to 2008; if house precedent wins, both stay 2007 and Forrest lives in judgement.

Safety-cell model identity and opener: the rabbit was never the safety model; the GLP tox package (rat/dog/monkey) was, and it is unpublished. Rule 6 wants a first-use-year opener, but there is no citable source for the tox package. Open with a placeholder (as the draft did, wrongly labelled), or omit (as the seed did)?

Competing non-preclinical model: human CETP-deficiency genetics predicted (inconsistently) before the rabbit was built on. The brief's 'best model = relied-on model' rule excludes it, and it is not a preclinical model; but should the atlas record a competing prediction anywhere structured, or only in judgement?

`magnitude` has no bin for a null or opposite result: rabbit 60% lesion reduction vs patient 0 is coded 'off_by_>5x', which reads as a scaling miss rather than an absent effect. Consider an 'absent'/'opposite' value.

`subjects` for de Grooth 2002: 'healthy subjects with mild hyperlipidemia' in a hyperlipidemia context; draft says healthy_volunteers (the paper's own wording), but they carry the context's disease. healthy_volunteers vs mixed?
